articles.title: Today in Crypto: Bitcoin Whales Accumulate, MiCA Register Revamp, AI Bug Bounties
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Bitcoin whales have added about 121,000 BTC since the end of September, defying historical year-end selling patterns. Meanwhile, the EU’s securities watchdog plans to make it easier to verify which crypto companies are authorized to operate in the bloc, and crypto bug bounty platforms are expanding their use of AI to identify genuine security threats amid a surge in submissions.
Bitcoin whales pile into BTC despite shrinking profit cushion
Bitcoin whales are bucking the years-long trend of trimming their balances toward the end of the year. Instead, they are accumulating the cryptocurrency despite falling prices and dwindling unrealized profits.
According to onchain analytics firm CryptoQuant, whales added about 121,000 Bitcoin (BTC) to their holdings between Sept. 30 and Nov. 21, taking their combined balance to nearly 2.95 million BTC, despite a price decline of nearly 30% over the same period.
CryptoQuant defines whales as addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC. Unrealized profits across addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have shrunk 81% to $23.8 billion from $124.7 billion on Sept. 30.
The report, supported by crypto lending platform CoinRabbit, notes that whales have historically reduced their holdings toward the end of the year in both bull and bear markets. Since 2017, whale balances have declined in seven of the nine previous fourth quarters, with 2019 and 2020 being the only exceptions.
Meanwhile, dolphins, a term referring to addresses holding between 100 and 1,000 BTC, have slightly reduced their holdings. The group shed about 15,169 BTC, representing 0.28% of its holdings.
ESMA to overhaul EU’s MiCA crypto register in 2027
The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) is preparing an overhaul of its public crypto register nearly two years after its launch.
The European Union’s securities watchdog plans to replace its manual interim register under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) with a searchable web-based platform around mid-2027, an ESMA spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
The new system will also maintain a version history for individual white papers to provide archives of changes.
MiCA’s transitional period ended in July, which meant that unauthorized crypto service providers had to wind down their EU operations or face multimillion-euro fines or other enforcement action. ESMA’s interim register serves as a public reference point for checking whether a crypto company is authorized in the bloc.
AI is driving a flood of crypto bug reports. Now it’s helping sort them
Crypto bug bounty platforms have expanded their use of artificial intelligence to keep up with a growing mountain of AI-assisted security reports.
Crypto-focused HackenProof said in October that it was using AI to triage 70% of submissions fully autonomously, aiming to hit 85% by the end of 2026. It said it received an average of about 6,100 bug reports a month in the third quarter, 2.4 times the reports from December last year.
Rival Immunefi last week said submissions to its platform rose 136% year-over-year in the first nine months of 2026, as it introduced a tool that can flag duplicates before a researcher submits a report.
Bug bounty programs pay independent researchers to find and report potential security flaws. AI has helped researchers uncover more genuine vulnerabilities, but has also swelled the volume of invalid and duplicate submissions, making it harder for security teams to identify the threats that need urgent attention.
It’s like “bringing a sword to a gunfight,” Dmitry Tokarev, founder of crypto wallet provider Bron, told Cointelegraph, referring to security teams that haven’t already adopted AI to sift through reports.

articles.title: Franklin Templeton Adds Hyperliquid’s HYPE to Crypto Index ETF
articles.text:
Franklin Templeton makes room for HYPE in crypto index ETF
The addition comes as US spot investment products tracking Hyperliquid’s native token reach $266.5 million in assets under management.
Asset manager Franklin Templeton plans to add the Hyperliquid (HYPE) token to its crypto index exchange-traded fund (ETF), according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Nov. 25.
The token will be added to the Franklin Crypto Index ETF on Dec. 1, following HYPE’s inclusion in the fund’s benchmark. The fund, which trades under the ticker EZPZ, currently holds Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH), XRP, Solana (SOL), Dogecoin (DOGE), Cardano (ADA) and Lumen (XLM).
Hyperliquid, a layer-1 blockchain that hosts a decentralized exchange specializing in perpetual futures trading, has seen its total value locked rise to $7.3 billion from $4.13 billion in early January. The protocol generated $80.3 million in revenue over the past 30 days, according to DefiLlama.
Its native token, HYPE, is used to pay network fees and can be staked to earn rewards. The protocol also uses a portion of its trading fee revenue to buy back HYPE on the open market, linking trading activity on the platform to demand for the token.
Related: HYPE teases all-time high as NYSE owner ICE eyes US Hyperliquid perps
HYPE expands its Wall Street footprint
Franklin Templeton’s move comes as more investment products offer exposure to HYPE.
Three US spot exchange-traded products (ETPs) tracking HYPE have launched since May, with offerings from asset managers 21Shares, Bitwise and Grayscale. They collectively held approximately $266.5 million in assets under management as of Nov. 27, according to Coinperps data.
These products allow US investors to gain exposure to the Hyperliquid ecosystem through traditional financial rails without having to directly hold the token.
The exchange ranks among the largest venues for decentralized perpetual futures trading, although its official interface remains restricted to US users. Perpetual futures are derivative contracts that allow traders to speculate on an asset’s price movements without a fixed expiration date.
President Donald Trump said in August that Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Michael Selig was working to bring Hyperliquid into the US in compliance with regulations.
Related: Hong Kong adds Hyperliquid to list of ‘suspicious’ crypto platforms

articles.title: Bitcoin Whales Buying Through Q4 Drawdown
articles.text:
Bitcoin whales pile into BTC despite shrinking profit cushion
CryptoQuant data shows Bitcoin whales are breaking with historical fourth-quarter selling patterns despite a market downturn.
Bitcoin whales are bucking the years-long trend of trimming their balances toward the end of the year. Instead, they are accumulating the cryptocurrency despite falling prices and dwindling unrealized profits.
According to onchain analytics firm CryptoQuant, whales added about 121,000 Bitcoin (BTC) to their holdings between Sept. 30 and Nov. 21, taking their combined balance to nearly 2.95 million BTC, despite a price decline of nearly 30% over the same period.
CryptoQuant defines whales as addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC. Unrealized profits across addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have shrunk 81% to $23.8 billion from $124.7 billion on Sept. 30.
The report, supported by crypto lending platform CoinRabbit, notes that whales have historically reduced their holdings toward the end of the year in both bull and bear markets. Since 2017, whale balances have declined in seven of the nine previous fourth quarters, with 2019 and 2020 being the only exceptions.
Meanwhile, dolphins, a term referring to addresses holding between 100 and 1,000 BTC, have slightly reduced their holdings. The group shed about 15,169 BTC, representing 0.28% of its holdings.
Related: Bitcoin supply metric hits 11-year low as new ‘capitulation’ signal arrives
Bitcoin loans may be taking the place of sales
The accumulation comes as Bitcoin has lost about 32% of its value since the beginning of the year, with the cryptocurrency trading at around $59,750 at 6:45 p.m. UTC on Friday, according to TradingView data. The report notes that borrowing against Bitcoin holdings may be allowing some large investors to access liquidity without selling their assets.
According to CryptoQuant, among CoinRabbit users with more than $100,000 in loans, the number of Bitcoin-backed loans increased by 298.9% month-on-month in October, while total loan volume fell by 16.2%.
The pattern contrasts with October 2025, when the number of Bitcoin-backed loans fell by 3.7% but total loan volume increased by 122.8%.
CryptoQuant suggested that the shift toward more frequent but smaller loans could indicate that large holders are borrowing to raise cash instead of selling Bitcoin.
Crypto tax firm Summ suggested the shift could also be linked to the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Since January, participating jurisdictions have begun requiring crypto exchanges and other service providers to collect users’ transaction data for tax authorities, with the first international exchanges of tax-related information expected in 2027.
Summ CEO Shane Brunette said holding BTC and borrowing against it are rational responses “to a world where every sale is visible.”

articles.title: China Issues New Rules for Blockchain-Based Digital Identities
articles.text:
China sets March 2027 rollout for blockchain identity regulations
China has issued new regulations governing blockchain-based digital identities, setting rules for cross-platform verification and data privacy.
China published new regulations on blockchain-based digital identities on Nov. 27, establishing a framework for identity verification and interoperability across government institutions and private-sector platforms.
The regulations, which will take effect on March 1, 2027, were jointly issued by 11 government departments, including the People’s Bank of China and the Cyberspace Administration of China.
Under the rules, China’s national blockchain network will provide the infrastructure for a digital identity system operated by entities authorized by the country’s cyberspace regulator, in cooperation with identity authentication and credential providers.
Digital identities powered by blockchain technology can allow users to verify their identity or credentials across platforms without disclosing unnecessary personal information.
According to Chinese state-backed media outlet China Net, the identity chain will bring together multiple institutions “to achieve multi-party consensus through blockchain technology.”
The regulations are part of China’s broader push to expand blockchain adoption, with the country targeting 2030 to largely complete its national blockchain infrastructure while maintaining restrictions on cryptocurrency-related activities in mainland China.
Limits on digital identity data collection
Individuals and organizations will be able to voluntarily register digital identities and use verifiable credentials to disclose specific information, such as educational or professional qualifications, without necessarily revealing all the associated data.
Platforms and digital identity service providers will be required to follow data minimization requirements, collecting only the information necessary for identity verification. They will be prohibited from using that data for cross-platform profiling or targeted advertising.
The regulations aim to address barriers to identity verification across regions, industries and platforms. They also encourage interoperability with digital yuan and the adoption of distributed digital identities in sectors including finance, taxation, transportation and customs.
Related: China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildout

articles.title: Bitcoin Stays Volatile as US Sellers Spark BTC Price Drop to $58,700
articles.text:
Bitcoin price drops below $59K as Anthropic joins tech stock rebound
Bitcoin price volatility returned at the Wall Street open as BTC/USD dropped to local lows of $58,700 while stocks and gold headed higher.
Bitcoin touched $62,100 on Friday as risk assets and precious metals rose during a shortened US trading session following the Thanksgiving holiday.
Key points:
- Bitcoin (BTC) experienced sudden volatility at Friday’s Wall Street open as sellers erased a move above $62,000.
- Crypto positions worth $228 million were liquidated in the hour ending at 3:00 p.m. UTC.
- Gold sought to cement its rebound after falling sharply below its 200-day moving average of $4,373 per ounce.
BTC price suddenly drops to $58,700
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD gaining up to 2.7% as US stock futures rose ahead of the Wall Street open. The pair then fell bellow $59,000 as sellers returned to the market following Thursday’s Thanksgiving closure of US stock markets.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Data from CoinGlass showed that $228 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the hour ending at 3:00 p.m. UTC.
BTC/USD vs. crypto liquidations. Source: CoinGlass
Traders appeared eager to increase tech-stock exposure during Friday’s shortened US trading session, with the closing bell due at 1:00 p.m. Eastern time. The S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index opened up 0.9% and 1.4%, respectively.
Tech stocks showed mixed performance, with Anthropic (Nasdaq: ANT) gaining 4% to trade above $87. The stock was about 18% higher than Wednesday’s low of $73.90.
Anthropic stock one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
At the same time, Nvidia shares fell 1.5% to $147 after the open.
“The hyperscalers ultimately have to get an ROI, and they ultimately need to rebuild their free cash flow, and people like Anthropic need to prove that they can generate the revenue growth that people expect and ultimately be very profitable and free-cash-flow generative as well,” Richard Clode, a portfolio manager at Janus Henderson, told CNBC.
Precious metals also rallied, with silver rising as much as 7.4% on the day, while gold (XAU/USD) was 2% higher at $3,635 per ounce as of 3 p.m. UTC.
XAU/USD one-day chart with the 200-day SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
On Wednesday, trading resource The Kobeissi Letter flagged highly oversold conditions in gold, which traded 20% below its 200-day simple moving average (SMA), currently at $4,373.
“This comes as gold prices have dropped -37% from their January intraday peak, their largest drawdown within a 12-month period since the early 1980s,” it wrote on X, calling gold’s 2026 retracement “one of its most severe declines in history.”
Analysis: Bitcoin “closer to seller capitulation”
Bitcoin price action diverged from stocks and precious metals as traders sold into the modest post-holiday gains.
Related: Crypto on notice as hawkish Fed risks December ‘meltdown’
Crypto trader and analyst Rekt Capital highlighted the intensity of the ongoing selling pressure on Bitcoin. “Since Bitcoin experienced a breakout on seller volume, Bitcoin’s price tumbled -27% to the downside,” the analyst wrote.
“Bitcoin has since also suffered 4 consecutive weeks of above-average sell-side volume, getting Bitcoin closer to seller capitulation & exhaustion.”
BTC/USD one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Previously, Cointelegraph reported that a growing share of the BTC supply was held at an unrealized loss as capitulation signals reappeared.

articles.title: What Coinbase’s Thanksgiving Trade Reveals About Tokenized Stocks
articles.text:
What was Coinbase worth while Nasdaq was closed?
A Thanksgiving buyer paid 106.24 USDC per Coinbase share. Whether that looked like a holiday rally depended on when you’d last checked the stock.
Tokenized stocks give investors another place to trade after the closing bell. Coinbase’s Thanksgiving tape shows why it still matters where else the shares changed hands and how many you want to trade.
On Thanksgiving afternoon, a buyer spent 125.49 USDC (USDC) on tokenized Coinbase shares while Nasdaq was closed. If you’d last checked the stock at Wednesday’s closing bell, that small purchase seemed to carry news of a holiday rally.
Coinbase had closed at $103.72, and the buyer on OKXICE paid 106.24 USDC per token, an apparent gain of 2.4%. But if you’d stayed for Wednesday’s after-hours session, you’d have seen the shares reach $106.91, according to brokerage Public.
From there, the very same token trade looked about 0.6% lower, valuing USDC at a dollar. However, the choice of where to start measuring was enough to turn a gain into a decline.
Related: Nasdaq exec pushes for common EU rules on tokenized securities
An investor in Germany had an even fresher price to go on. Early on Thanksgiving, 142 Coinbase shares changed hands on Tradegate at 97.50 euros apiece, roughly $107 at that day’s exchange rate.
What changed for the afternoon buyer was that they could open a wallet and buy Coinbase exposure over the holiday, and anyone following the stock could see exactly what that order cost.
Finding oneself on the other side of that trade with $10,000 worth of Coinbase to sell, the blockchain could tell you to four decimal places what someone had paid for just over one token, but could you get that price for 94?

articles.title: Binance Plans Tokenized IPO Launch After Regulatory Approval
articles.text:
Binance to launch tokenized IPO program after regulatory approval: Yi He
Binance is hiring for equity capital markets roles, including an analyst to develop tokenized equity products and assess prospective issuers.
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance plans to launch a tokenized initial public offering (IPO) program for onchain share issuance once it receives regulatory approval.
The project forms part of Binance’s real-world asset strategy and will involve collaboration with decentralized finance projects, Binance co-founder and co-CEO Yi He said during BNB Demo Night in Bangkok on Friday.
“Actually, that’s a professional IPO process,” He said, distinguishing the planned program from simply listing new assets on the exchange.
Her comments follow Binance’s recent job postings for equity capital markets roles, which fueled speculation about the exchange’s plans to facilitate onchain IPOs.
One job posting seeks an equity capital markets research analyst to help develop tokenized equity products, evaluate prospective issuers and assess deal structures, pricing and allocation. The role requires at least four years of relevant experience and an understanding of traditional IPOs and follow-on offerings.
Cointelegraph reached out to Binance for further details but had not received a response by publication.
Related: BNB Chain details new layer-1 for trading, private finance and AI

articles.title: Brazil’s Stock Exchange Targets 2027 Stablecoin Launch
articles.text:
Brazil’s stock exchange pushes stablecoin launch back to 2027
Brazil’s stock exchange is working with six major financial institutions on a real-backed stablecoin that could launch as early as the first quarter of 2027.
Brazil’s stock exchange B3 is moving ahead with 2027 plans for a stablecoin pegged to the Brazilian real, after initially targeting a launch this year.
B3 is collaborating with six of Brazil’s largest financial institutions, Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Itaú Unibanco, Safra, Santander and XP, to launch the stablecoin in the first quarter of 2027, according to a Friday report by local news outlet Valor Econômico.
Called Open BRL, the stablecoin is to be issued by Banco B3, the exchange’s banking subsidiary, with each token backed by one Brazilian real. B3 will operate the underlying technology.
The initiative marks a new stage in the exchange’s digital asset strategy as Brazil’s financial industry prepares to bring traditional securities onto blockchain networks.
B3’s stablecoin plans stretch into 2027
B3 first disclosed plans to introduce its own stablecoin in December 2025, targeting a launch in 2026.
As recently as July, the exchange was reportedly still preparing to launch a stablecoin called B3RL in the coming months, with infrastructure testing and integration with financial institutions scheduled for August and September.
B3RL was designed to be backed by Brazilian reais and secured by government bonds, and to facilitate blockchain-based trading of stocks and fixed-income securities starting in 2027.
It remains unclear whether Open BRL will replace B3RL or operate alongside it. Cointelegraph reached out to B3 for clarification but had not received a response by publication.
Tokenized stocks face regulatory hurdles
B3 also plans to introduce trading of tokenized shares in early 2027, initially using the same order book as conventional equities.
The platform would initially retain its two-business-day settlement cycle rather than introduce instant settlement, Humberto Costa, a B3 executive overseeing digital asset products, reportedly said in October.
Related: Brazil’s Halloween eve crypto deadline brings more tricks than treats
Costa also said B3RL would not handle settlement of tokenized shares at launch and that round-the-clock trading would require changes to Brazil’s regulatory framework.
Brazil’s Securities and Exchange Commission has been exploring a new regulatory framework for tokenization, presenting the progress of its dedicated working group at an industry meeting in October.

articles.title: OpenAI Turns the Tables on Apple With Its Own Trade-Secret Theft Claims
articles.text:
In brief
- OpenAI countersued Apple on Friday in California federal court, accusing the iPhone maker of stealing its trade secrets and “coercing and threatening” hardware suppliers that work with both companies.
- The counterclaims—federal trade-secret theft, contract interference and unfair competition—invert Apple’s July lawsuit, which alleged two former Apple employees carried confidential hardware files to OpenAI.
- Apple says its probe found no OpenAI secrets, and its suit goes to trial in July 2027.
OpenAI has turned the tables on Apple, filing a countersuit that accuses the iPhone maker of stealing its trade secrets and pressuring hardware suppliers to freeze the ChatGPT maker out, escalating a legal brawl over the race to build the next must-have AI gadget.
The counterclaims, filed Friday in federal court in San Jose, California, flip the script on a dispute Apple started in July, when it sued OpenAI, its io Products hardware unit and two former Apple employees, Tang Tan and Chang Liu, accusing them of carrying confidential hardware secrets to OpenAI to help build a competing device.
OpenAI denied those claims and cast Apple’s suit as an attempt to choke off its ability to hire Apple talent.
Did you know?

Now OpenAI is alleging misconduct of Apple’s own. In the filing, the company accuses Apple of “coercing and threatening” suppliers that work with both firms, including asking shared manufacturers to identify which personnel were assigned to OpenAI projects and pressuring at least one vendor to stop work.
OpenAI also claims a former OpenAI employee who returned to Apple took details about its product plans and suppliers with them, an inversion of Apple’s original accusation.
The countersuit brings claims including federal trade-secret theft, interference with contracts and unfair competition under California law. OpenAI argues Apple sued because it is losing the AI race, asserting in the complaint that the company “has struggled to incorporate innovative AI capabilities into its previously popular products” and is trying to “compete unfairly by any means available.”
It also contends Apple’s employment and exit policies create “trapdoors” designed to let it accuse departing staff of theft.
The reciprocal accusations underscore how high the stakes have climbed in the contest to define the hardware of the AI era. The earlier phase of the case grew contentious over discovery, with OpenAI’s internal emails and text messages drawn into the fight.
A judge indicated the court was “highly likely” to grant Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction, and in October OpenAI pledged not to use the Apple trade secrets at the center of the suit.
Apple has previously said its investigation turned up no OpenAI confidential information. Its original lawsuit is set for trial on July 19, 2027.

articles.title: Could AI Break Bitcoin? Not Yet, Research Firm K33 Says
articles.text:
In brief
- Research firm K33 said AI’s rapid math progress warrants attention to Bitcoin’s cryptography, but recent breakthroughs have not shown the network’s security is broken.
- Bitcoin’s elliptic-curve signatures rest on the unsolved “P versus NP” problem.
- The report lands as the Ethereum Foundation, flagged AI as more urgent than quantum, doubles its security team and targets a 2029 post-quantum transition.
Recent AI-assisted advances in mathematics have reignited worries about the cryptography underpinning Bitcoin, but there’s no evidence the network’s security has actually been broken, according to a report from research and brokerage firm K33.
The analysts, writing Friday, said AI’s rapid progress in math warrants closer attention to Bitcoin’s defenses, while cautioning against mistaking theoretical breakthroughs for a practical attack.
“Naturally, this has reignited fears surrounding the mathematical assumptions underpinning Bitcoin and modern cryptography,” they wrote, adding that the developments do not themselves offer a way to crack those systems.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
The spark was a draft proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, one of math’s most famous open problems, published last week by Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge with help from the company’s Claude model.
As Decrypt reported, the proof passed independent computational verification, though academic review is ongoing. Its arrival stoked speculation about whether AI could eventually unravel the math securing digital assets.
K33 pushed back on the alarm. Bitcoin’s transaction signatures rely on elliptic curve cryptography, which hinges on how hard it is to derive a private key from a public one, even though the reverse is easy.
The firm noted that the Riemann proof provides no method for attacking that, and that the deeper “P versus NP” question at the heart of such fears remains unsolved. Even if someone proved P equals NP, K33 said, that wouldn’t necessarily yield a usable algorithm, or one that could run fast enough to recover a private key in any practical timeframe.
Conversely, proving P does not equal NP wouldn’t guarantee Bitcoin’s safety either, since faster attack algorithms could still emerge.
The report lands as the broader industry takes the AI-cryptography threat increasingly seriously. The Ethereum Foundation recently flagged AI as a more urgent danger than quantum computing, given its ability to find software flaws and sharpen existing algorithms.
K33 noted the Ethereum Foundation has doubled its protocol security team and recommended the Keccak-256 hash function for a post-quantum transition it aims to complete by 2029.
The takeaway, per K33, is vigilance without panic.
AI’s mathematical leaps deserve monitoring, and crypto networks are right to harden their cryptography against future threats, but as things stand, Bitcoin’s defenses remain as sound as they were at launch, with no demonstrated compromise.

articles.title: Austria-Supervised Crypto Firms Report 20.4B Euros in H1 Trading Volume
articles.text:
Austria-supervised crypto firms report 20.4B euros in H1 trading volume
About 74% of accounts were based in other EEA countries, highlighting the market’s cross-border nature and putting Europe’s supervisory framework in focus, FMA said.
Crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) supervised by the Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) reported 20.4 billion euros ($22.37 billion) in trading volume for the first half of 2026.
About 74% of user accounts on these platforms were based in other European Economic Area (EEA) countries, particularly Germany and France, the Austrian financial supervisor said in a press release on Friday.
The 20.4 billion euros in the first half of 2026 exceeded the 17 billion euros reported for the full year of 2025, according to the FMA’s annual report.
The FMA said increasing cross-border activity creates a sharp focus on Europe’s crypto supervisory framework and highlights ongoing discussions about giving the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) an enhanced supervisory role over the industry.
In December 2025, the European Commission proposed transfering “direct supervisory competences” for key pieces of market infrastructure, including CASPs, to ESMA. If adopted by EU lawmakers, ESMA’s role in overseeing EU capital markets would resemble the framework of the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
In September 2025, France became the third European country to call for ESMA to take over supervision of major crypto firms, joining Austrian and Italian securities regulators.

articles.title: 4 Scary Bitcoin Charts That Suggest This Bear Market Is Different
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday, trading more than 52% below its all-time high as its daily technical indicators remain bearish.
- Bitcoin has slipped below Bitbo's Power Law support line and the lowest colored band of the Rainbow Chart.
- Four popular Bitcoin valuation models suggest theoretical prices ranging from $141,000 to nearly $400,000, substantially above its actual market price.
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 again on Friday as roughly $6.8 billion worth of Bitcoin options expired on derivatives exchange Deribit earlier in the day.
The largest cryptocurrency by market cap was trading at around $59,576 as of writing, down 1.58% on the daily chart after reaching an intraday high of $62,210.
As you might be able to guess based on the recent price action, Bitcoin's technical setup remains bearish—and there’s four charts in particular that tell the story.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
The coin is trading well below its 50-day and 200-day exponential moving averages, or EMAs, which currently sit at $71,112 and $74,444, respectively, with the shorter-term average below the longer-term one—a classically bearish death cross pattern.
Its Relative Strength Index, or RSI, which measures the strength of recent price movements on a scale of 0 to 100, sits at 25.69, putting Bitcoin in oversold territory. Bitcoin is also approaching its 61.8% Fibonacci retracement level at $57,618, a potential support derived from the cryptocurrency's rally between its 2022 bottom and 2025 peak.
A sustained break below that level would put the recent lows back in focus. The next major Fibonacci retracement on the chart sits near $39,000, which would be an absolute nightmare for the markets. Thankfully for Bitcoin holders, BTC has bounced every time it touched it.
Perhaps more concerning for long-term Bitcoin investors, however, is what's happening to some of the most popular models used to make sense of Bitcoin's historical price cycles.
Bitcoin breaks its power law floor
The Bitcoin Power Law model, popularized by physicist Giovanni Santostasi, attempts to explain Bitcoin's price growth as a mathematical function of its age.
Plotting Bitcoin's price and the time elapsed since its creation on logarithmic scales produces a relatively straight trend line. Two parallel lines establish theoretical upper and lower boundaries based on historical price extremes.
The appeal of the model was that Bitcoin's increasingly expensive bear market bottoms appeared remarkably predictable, despite the cryptocurrency's notorious volatility.
Bitcoin is now trading below what crypto analytics provider Bitbo sets as the theoretical support line of approximately $68,600, while the model's central regression puts its price near $193,400.
That's roughly 69% below its theoretical valuation, and 13% below what was supposed to be its historical floor.
The breach challenges one of the model's most attractive assumptions: that Bitcoin's minimum price increases predictably over time.
Bitcoin's worst post-halving performance
Bitcoin's four-year market cycle revolves around the halving, a programmed event that cuts the issuance of new Bitcoin tokens by 50% approximately every four years.
The most recent halving, in April 2024, reduced the reward miners receive for producing a block from 6.25 BTC to 3.125 BTC.
Bitbo's post-halving comparison chart takes the price performance following the 2012, 2016 and 2020 halvings and adjusts those returns to Bitcoin's price at the start of the 2024 cycle.
Had Bitcoin replicated its performance following the 2020 halving, it would currently be trading somewhere around $140,000. Matching the returns of its earlier cycles would imply prices of several hundred thousand dollars or more.
Instead, roughly 950 days after its most recent halving, Bitcoin is trading below where it was when that cycle began.
Diminishing returns are nothing new for Bitcoin as the asset grows larger. But the scale of the current underperformance raises questions about how useful previous halving cycles remain as a guide to future returns.
It also shows traders are a bit less enthusiastic about the upcoming halving vs previous times—maybe because Bitcoin is now more mainstream and the user base is more diverse and less interested in those technicalities.
Somewhere under the Rainbow
The Bitcoin Rainbow Chart, which originated in 2014, uses logarithmic price curves and colored bands to classify Bitcoin's historical valuation.
The upper red bands represent speculative bubbles, while the lower blue and violet bands indicate historically depressed prices.
Bitcoin's price has dropped beneath even the violet region, humorously labeled “Bitcoin Dead,” in the supplied chart.
This isn't the first time the Rainbow Chart has struggled to accommodate Bitcoin's price movements. Its creator revised the model in November 2022 after the previous version failed to contain that year's market collapse.
The chart is ultimately a visualization of historical price behavior rather than a scientifically validated valuation model. Its latest divergence is another reminder of that limitation.
Four price models, and none come close
Bitbo's price prediction comparison brings together four different approaches to estimating Bitcoin's long-term value.
The Stock-to-Flow model, introduced by pseudonymous analyst PlanB in 2019, measures scarcity by comparing Bitcoin's existing supply with its annual issuance. Stock-to-Income expands on that concept by incorporating miners' transaction fee revenue and regularly updating its calculations.
The Power Law measures price growth over time, while the Halving Price Regression fits a curve using historical prices at halving dates, excluding much of the speculative activity between them.
In the chart's late-2026 projections, Stock-to-Flow puts Bitcoin near $397,535, followed by the Power Law at $198,495, Stock-to-Income at $173,412, and Halving Price Regression at $141,132.
Bitcoin is trading approximately 85% below the most optimistic of those projections and 58% below even the most conservative one.
None of these models directly measures how much money investors are willing to put into Bitcoin today, and arguably Bitcoin is now a different asset than the BTC we used to follow two years ago.
It’s possible that after the wave of ETFs, funds, derivatives, 401Ks, regulations, indicators tracking its price, and widespread access to retail investors, it’s these price-prediction models that need to change.
After all, Bitcoin already did.

articles.title: Bitcoin Supply Profit/Loss Ratio Hits Lowest Level Since 2015
articles.text:
Bitcoin supply metric hits 11-year low as new ‘capitulation’ signal arrives
The seven-day moving average of Bitcoin’s supply profit/loss ratio hit an 11-year low as BTC price losses month-to-date remain near 20%.
Bitcoin (BTC) is in a “meaningful stress phase” as an onchain profit-to-loss metric hits its lowest levels in 11 years.
Key points:
- Bitcoin’s supply in profit/loss ratio dropped to 0.825 on Nov. 26, its lowest level since September 2015 on a seven-day moving average basis.
- Sell-side risk has fallen to 16.52 on a rolling 30-day basis, a level rarely seen outside bear-market bottoms.
- Analysis from CryptoQuant pointed to increasing signs of seller exhaustion.
Bitcoin supply profit ratio drops to 2015 levels
Data from onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant reveals that Bitcoin on Thursday recorded its largest unrealized loss skew in more than 11 years.
The seven-day moving average of Bitcoin’s supply in profit/loss ratio has fallen to 0.825, below its parity level of 1. Values below 1 reflect a market state in which loss-making supply outweighs supply in profit.
The metric’s 30-day moving average remains higher at 1.27, reflecting the influence of recent price action on supply profitability. BTC/USD recorded its largest month-to-date loss of 28.8% as it dipped to $55,081 on Nov. 21.
“Historically, comparable conditions have appeared near major market bottoms, including the 2022 bear market,” CryptoQuant contributor CryptoZeno wrote Friday.
“However, the 7 day and 30 day averages still need to stabilize and recover above the threshold before a durable improvement can be confirmed.”
Bitcoin supply in profit/loss. Source: CryptoQuant
Low sell-side risk amid fresh 2026 “capitulation”
Bitcoin’s sell-side risk ratio, which divides total onchain realized profit and loss by the realized cap, has dropped to levels that typically accompany bear-market bottoms. Its 30-day moving average currently measures 16.52, reflecting a period of “capitulation” among investors.
Related: Crypto on notice as hawkish Fed risks December ‘meltdown’
Sell-side risk treats any onchain movement as a source of potential selling pressure, and low values imply increasing seller exhaustion at current prices around $60,000. Bitcoin has seen several capitulation phases in 2026, its first since the end of the 2022 bear market.
Bitcoin sell-side risk ratio. Source: CryptoQuant
Previously, Cointelegraph reported on an increasing profitability squeeze affecting both short-term and long-term Bitcoin hodlers. The realized price of the extant supply, the price at which it last moved onchain, currently sits near $53,200 and forms a target of interest based on previous bear markets.

articles.title: $7 Billion in Bitcoin Options Just Expired: Here’s What It Means
articles.text:
In brief
- Nearly $6.8 billion in Bitcoin options expired Friday on Deribit, representing roughly a quarter of outstanding Bitcoin options positions.
- Traders have shifted toward downside protection since October, with substantial put positions extending as low as $40,000.
- U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded $5.39 billion in net outflows this November, putting them on track for their worst month since launching.
Nearly $6.8 billion worth of Bitcoin options expired Friday on crypto derivatives exchange Deribit, removing roughly a quarter of outstanding Bitcoin options positions from the exchange, according to CryptoQuant.
The expiration comes at a particularly difficult time for Bitcoin. The cryptocurrency traded near $61,000 ahead of settlement before dropping below $59,000 later Friday, extending a brutal November for crypto investors.
Friday’s expiry was considerably smaller than October’s $10.8 billion settlement, but the way traders positioned themselves tells a different story about market sentiment.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Options are financial contracts that give investors the right to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price, known as the strike price. Call options generally benefit from rising prices, whereas put options can serve as insurance against a decline.
Nearly half of the outstanding $40,000 put positions were scheduled to expire on December 25. That doesn't necessarily mean traders expect Bitcoin to fall that far, but it shows that investors are willing to position themselves against such a scenario.
What happens after the expiry?
The estimated “max pain” price for Friday’s expiration stood at $70,000. That's the price at which option holders collectively receive the smallest payout at expiration, around 15% above Bitcoin’s price heading into settlement.
Bitcoin settled at approximately $61,600, leaving many put options with intrinsic value and higher-priced calls worthless.
The expiration does not mean $6.8 billion in Bitcoin changed hands. That figure is just the notional value of the underlying contracts, rather than the amount paid out at expiration.
What could affect Bitcoin's price is the unwinding of positions that market makers accumulated to offset their exposure to those contracts. As those hedges become unnecessary, buying or selling activity associated with them can disappear or reverse, potentially amplifying price movements in either direction.
Bitcoin still faces considerable selling pressure outside the derivatives market.
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs registered their seventh consecutive trading session of net withdrawals on Wednesday, bringing November’s total to $5.39 billion.
Accelerating inflation, concerns over U.S. interest rates, and a renewed AI stock selloff have also put pressure on Bitcoin this week.
Traders were paying more for near-term volatility than for volatility further into 2027 ahead of the expiry, which likely means that concerns about Bitcoin’s near-term performance extend well beyond Friday’s settlement.
The next major options expiry is scheduled for Christmas Day, with contracts covering roughly 165,000 BTC, or about $10 billion at Friday’s settlement price.

articles.title: Bluefin to Shut Down Perps, Refocus on Spot Trading and Tokenized RWAs
articles.text:
Bluefin to shut down perps, refocus on spot trading and tokenized RWAs
Bluefin will close its perps platform on Dec. 4, exiting a shrinking Sui market where it once handled over $500 million in daily trades.
Bluefin will discontinue its perpetual futures trading services on Dec. 4 to redirect resources toward spot trading and tokenized real-world assets.
“As the Sui team internalizes more of the network’s perps initiatives, we believe Bluefin’s resources are best focused on opportunities that complement that direction,” the decentralized exchange announced in a Thursday X post.
The platform urged users to close open positions by Dec. 4 and said withdrawals will remain available for an undetermined period after trading ends.
Bluefin said it accounted for 95% of Sui’s all-time perpetual trading volume and had more than 2.5 million accounts.
Bluefin handled as much as $575 million in perpetual futures trades on Feb. 14, 2024. The single-day volume dropped to $516,253 on Friday, according to DefiLlama data.
Bluefin is exiting a Sui perpetual futures market already experiencing a downturn. The network’s monthly perps volume has fallen from a peak of $4.85 billion in December 2024 to $312 million so far in November, according to DefiLlama.

articles.title: Binance withdrawals are back after October’s hack and here’s why yours might still be blocked
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Binance said on Nov. 26 that it lifted the withdrawal suspension imposed after its October security incident.
- The exchange said maintenance or planned upgrades still paused withdrawals on a small number of networks when it issued the update.
- Customers can check withdrawal status for their chosen asset and network and read any account alert for separate restrictions.
On Nov. 26, Binance said it had lifted the withdrawal freeze imposed after its October hack, but customers moving crypto to their own wallets may still encounter pauses on individual networks or account restrictions.
In its recovery update, the exchange said withdrawals on a small number of networks were still paused for maintenance or planned upgrades.
Binance described those pauses as routine and separate from the work it did to restore withdrawals after the hack.
How to check a delayed Binance withdrawal
Open Binance’s withdrawal screen for the asset you want to send and check the status of the network you plan to use. You can also check that asset and network on Binance’s public network status page.
Binance’s withdrawal suspension FAQ says wallet maintenance can temporarily stop withdrawals, and a network upgrade can make withdrawals of a particular asset unavailable.
For an upgrade-related pause, the FAQ says the withdrawal screen shows the reason and an estimated recovery time. Customers can set a reminder on that screen to get a status update.
A restriction on your account’s withdrawal function requires a different check, so the next step is to review the account alert for the reason and next steps.
An asset may show an available withdrawal route while the account still has a hold. In that case, the status page answers the route question, and the notice on your account tells you what action Binance needs from you.
Binance’s account guide says some security actions, including changing a password, can trigger a temporary withdrawal hold. Depending on the restriction, the alert may ask you to complete verification or offer an appeal.
The Nov. 26 notice also warned customers about messages promising to speed up a withdrawal. Binance says it will never ask for your password, two-factor authentication code, or wallet seed phrase. If someone contacts you about a delay, go directly to the Binance app or website for support.
The latest update closes a phased reopening that had already begun before Nov. 26. On Nov. 13, Binance restored access on some networks and was still working to reopen other routes, even after the exchange said it had replaced the customer assets lost in the hack.

articles.title: ESMA to Overhaul EU MiCA Crypto Register in 2027
articles.text:
ESMA to overhaul EU’s MiCA crypto register in 2027
ESMA’s new MiCA register will replace manual reporting and introduce automated data checks and a version history for crypto white papers.
The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) is preparing an overhaul of its public crypto register nearly two years after its launch.
The European Union’s securities watchdog plans to replace its manual interim register under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) with a searchable web-based platform around mid-2027, an ESMA spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
The new system will also maintain a version history for individual white papers to provide archives of changes.
MiCA’s transitional period ended in July, which meant that unauthorized crypto service providers had to wind down their EU operations or face multimillion-euro fines or other enforcement action. ESMA’s interim register serves as a public reference point for checking whether a crypto company is authorized in the bloc.
ESMA to move away from manual email reporting
ESMA launched its interim register in December 2024, publishing downloadable spreadsheet files containing information supplied by national regulators.
“The new IT system will replace the current manual email-based submission and consolidation process with a structured web-based interface through which national competent authorities can provide and update information for their relevant entities/white papers,” ESMA said.
The system will also be able to cross-check information against reference databases, including the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF) registry, which maintains a global database of legal entity identifiers.
For white papers, the system will perform technical checks against ESMA’s standardized reporting framework, helping identify missing mandatory information and documents that do not meet formatting requirements.
New MiCA register to host white papers directly
Another major change concerns how investors access crypto white papers, which outline information about crypto assets, their issuers and associated risks.
“The future register will not rely solely on links to white papers hosted on an entity’s website as is currently the case with the interim solution,” the ESMA spokesperson said, adding: “In the new IT solution, the white papers will be available directly on the register platform.”
Related: Spain moves to grant financial watchdog power to freeze crypto accounts
Users will also be able to download register data in CSV format or retrieve it through application programming interfaces (APIs), although ESMA said it could not yet disclose the full range of planned features.
Addressing the timing of the overhaul, the spokesperson said the development schedule was unrelated to the end of MiCA’s transitional period or the ongoing review of the regulation, adding:
“The timeline is driven entirely by technical development.”

articles.title: Hackers Hit US Air Force Cloud System Running Air-Defense and Munitions Data
articles.text:
In brief
- Hackers breached Cloud One, the U.S. Air Force’s flagship cloud platform, potentially exposing sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.
- Launched in 2017 and pooling Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet resources, Cloud One supports systems including air-defense command and control and global munitions tracking.
- It’s unclear who’s behind it or whether data was stolen.
Hackers have breached Cloud One, the U.S. Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, potentially jeopardizing a vast trove of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data, according to a Reuters report Friday that cited three people familiar with the matter.
The intrusion was discovered within the past month during work to upgrade the system, the report said, and investigators have called in U.S. Cyber Command, the military’s cyber force, to assess the damage.
“A breach here is a big deal,” one source told Reuters. It remains unclear who was behind the attack, how deeply they penetrated the system, or whether any data was stolen; the Air Force declined to comment on the specifics.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic, Nvidia, Microsoft and more with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Launched in 2017, Cloud One was built as a one-stop shop for the Air Force’s IT needs, pooling resources from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet to run scores of applications.
Among the systems it supports are the Air Force’s Cloud-Based Command and Control, which collates air-defense radar and other data feeds across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles at more than 200 Air Force locations worldwide.
One source said intruders reached the platform’s control plane by exploiting a software flaw, though it’s not confirmed whether they took further action from there.
The breach has triggered real disruption. Officials paused ongoing migrations of back-office software to the platform, revoked administrator rights for some users, and blocked updates to existing applications, leaving personnel unable to apply fixes just as a fresh batch of serious software vulnerabilities was disclosed across the tech industry.
The incident lands amid a jittery stretch of cyberattacks and outages hitting U.S. federal institutions. Earlier this week, the CIA, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence disclosed a breach of some unclassified systems, an intrusion investigators have tied to a suspected AI-powered hacking tool known as Artex.
That case fed growing alarm that artificial intelligence is accelerating the scale and sophistication of state-level intrusions, a concern now hanging over the Cloud One breach as well, even as its origin remains unknown.
For now, the Air Force says it continues to take “prudent measures” to protect its systems and mission capabilities, while the full scope of what was accessed, and by whom, remains under investigation.

articles.title: New York AG Secures $1.37B Court Judgment against NovaTech Founders
articles.text:
New York AG secures $1.37B court judgment against NovaTech founders
The judgment follows an August 2025 default ruling against the founders over a Ponzi scheme that targeted Haitian and other immigrant communities.
New York Attorney General Letitia James secured a $1.367 billion court judgment against Cynthia and Eddy Petion, the founders of defunct crypto and forex trading company NovaTech, over an investment scheme that defrauded hundreds of thousands of people.
“Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said in a Wednesday press release.
In October, James sought a court order for the Petions and affiliated companies to pay about $1.37 billion, including $1.13 billion in investor funds and $232.5 million in interest. The request followed a default judgment issued in August 2025, which found the company and its founders liable by default after the couple fled the country and failed to respond to the lawsuit.
James sued NovaTech in June 2024, alleging that the platform targeted immigrant communities, particularly Haitian New Yorkers, through prayer groups and social media, promising high returns on investments. Over 11,000 New Yorkers lost tens of millions of dollars to NovaTech and an earlier crypto mining scheme, AWS Mining.
AWS Mining collapsed in 2019, while NovaTech followed suit in 2023.
Related: SEC charges 8 firms over fake crypto platforms tied to $37M fraud

articles.title: Nvidia's Blackwell Chips Turn Up in China as Trump Floats Government Stake
articles.text:
In brief
- Nvidia Blackwell chips, which cannot be shipped to China without a U.S. license, were installed at a Shanghai data center tied to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reported.
- President Trump told the New York Post he had considered taking a government stake in Nvidia, as Washington did with Intel, and that "it's probably not too late."
- Nvidia shares were little changed at about $149 on Friday, down roughly 10% from Monday's close after Jensen Huang's reinstatement.
Nvidia's most powerful chips have turned up at a Chinese data center tied to Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the scandal surrounding the company, as U.S. President Donald Trump said he could still take a government stake in the chipmaker.
Two Chinese firms installed Nvidia Blackwell hardware at the Yangtze River Delta Project, a data center in Shanghai, according to documents submitted to Chinese regulators and reviewed by Bloomberg. Blackwell chips have always required a U.S. license to ship to China.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short NVDA with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
One of the firms, Shanghai Shuoyao, offered a GB300 NVL72 rack, which contains 72 Blackwell Ultra chips, as collateral for a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, Bloomberg reported. Another, Shanghai Kezhan, described a GB200 server at the site when it took out a 90 million yuan loan from a leasing firm owned by a Shanghai government agency in late 2025. Kezhan's majority owner is a Tokyo firm that Chinese outlet Caixin has said is controlled by Alice Huang.
Using the rack's serial number, Bloomberg found it was built by Taiwan's Gigabyte, which declined to say whom it originally sold the hardware to. It's unclear how the rack reached China. Shanghai Shuoyao has said it is one of Megaspeed's service providers, describing the relationship as "limited to ordinary commercial cooperation." Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company Alice Huang founded, has denied wrongdoing, and Bloomberg said it had no evidence that Megaspeed diverted hardware to the site. Nvidia did not respond to Bloomberg's questions.
Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence suspects of working with Chinese intelligence during an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, is at the center of a scandal that briefly cost him his job. The Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist this week.
Trump eyes a stake
Trump, who has said he "convinced" Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang, told the New York Post he was open to the U.S. government taking an equity stake in Nvidia, pointing to Intel, which handed Washington 10% of the company last year.
"I thought about it. I said, 'You know, maybe I should do it,' but I didn't bring it up at this point. It's probably not too late," Trump said.
He also said a pardon for Huang was "always an option" but that he didn't think it would be necessary, and urged Huang not to invoke his Fifth Amendment rights when he appears before Congress next week. Huang is due to sit for a closed-door interview with three House committees on December 1, and to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3.
Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate on Friday, Trump again said Huang was not a security threat. Asked by AFP how he could be sure when the Justice Department would not confirm it had conducted a thorough investigation, Trump said his view was based on "information I have, which is a lot of information," The Straits Times reported. "I think he's absolutely fine," he said.
Polling analyst Nate Silver said on his podcast that Trump "absolutely" could be removed from office if he profited from selling advanced chips to China, and that a roughly 25% chance of impeachment and removal priced by prediction markets was "entirely reasonable."
On Polymarket, traders put a 20% chance on Trump being impeached and removed before 2028, and a 74% chance on him being impeached before his term ends. Kalshi priced a 21% chance of Trump being impeached and removed before his term ends in January 2029.
Nvidia shares were trading at $148.74 on Friday, down 0.4% on the day, according to Yahoo! Finance. That leaves them almost 10% below Monday's close of $165.05, when the stock jumped more than 30% on Huang's return.

articles.title: Israeli bank lets customers buy Bitcoin but charges them 2% to get in and 2% to get out
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Discount Bank opened in-app Bitcoin and Ethereum trading on Nov. 26 for eligible Israeli retail customers.
- The bank blocks external crypto transfers and credits sale proceeds in US dollars the next business day.
- Discount Bank charges 2% on every buy or sell, with any applicable currency conversion fee charged separately.
Israel Discount Bank opened Bitcoin and Ethereum trading in its retail banking app on Nov. 26, letting eligible customers buy, hold, and sell the two assets through their securities account.
The service blocks transfers to private wallets and outside institutions. To cash out, customers sell in the app, and the bank credits US dollars to their account.
The bank’s product FAQ says the service is available to Israeli residents aged 18 and older who have signed up for securities trading with Discount Bank.
Customers then accept a separate crypto trading agreement in the app to place orders through the existing account and see the holdings alongside their other investments.
How customers cash out Bitcoin and Ethereum
Customers who already hold Bitcoin or Ethereum elsewhere can’t bring those coins into the service, so the account serves as both the place to trade and the place where customers see their crypto holdings.
The bank credits sale proceeds in US dollars the next business day, and customers who want shekels or another currency can ask the bank to convert them.
The bank lists dealing hours of 9 a.m. to 11 p.m.; the app accepts orders for immediate execution only during those hours. Market conditions, insufficient liquidity, blockchain congestion, or technical problems can limit execution.
The bank’s Nov. 11 announcement said it holds customer assets in bank wallets that use Fireblocks infrastructure. The FAQ says licensed third parties provide the service and custody.
Discount Bank waives custody fees for six months after the Nov. 26 launch, then lists a custody fee of 0.25% per quarter.
Trading carries a separate 2% charge on each buy and sell. Customers who buy and later sell pay that commission on both transactions, with each charge based on the transaction value.
For customers who want to convert the resulting dollars into shekels, any applicable currency conversion fee is added to the sale commission.

articles.title: Japan’s Crypto Industry Taps SEAL to Combat Hacks
articles.text:
Japan’s crypto security group taps SEAL to speed up hack response
The partnership comes weeks after a third-party data breach exposed hundreds of thousands of customer email addresses belonging to two Japanese crypto exchanges.
Japan’s crypto industry cybersecurity group has signed an agreement with US nonprofit Security Alliance (SEAL) to improve the detection of cyberattacks and respond to incidents more effectively.
According to a statement released Friday, the memorandum will see JPCrypto-ISAC receive help from SEAL to develop an incident response support framework and give them access to SEAL’s incident response and support capabilities. Both organizations will also share cyber threat intelligence.
In the Web3 and digital asset sector, addressing cyber threats that transcend national borders has become essential, said JPCrypto-ISAC representative director Naoji Noda. “We are delighted to establish this partnership with SEAL through this MOU.”
JPCrypto-ISAC had 16 full members at launch in 2025, including SBI VC Trade, bitbank, GMO Coin and Rakuten Wallet. The organization helps Japanese crypto companies share and analyze cyber threat intelligence.
Earlier this month, Japanese crypto exchanges Zaif and CoinTrade disclosed that a breach at their email provider, Arara, exposed hundreds of thousands of customer email addresses.
Arara estimated that the breach may have affected up to 380 companies across its customer base.
Japan’s crypto industry suffered a major breach in May 2024, when hackers stole Bitcoin worth about $305 million at the time from crypto exchange DMM Bitcoin. US and Japanese authorities later attributed the theft to North Korean hackers.
Related: Hackers breach CIA intelligence network in latest US cyberattack

articles.title: Chainflip identifies who lost money in $12.6 million hack as recovery plan takes shape
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Chainflip says it identified affected swappers, account holders and liquidity providers after the Nov. 21 vault theft.
- Chainflip says it will use prices from the time of the attack to settle outstanding loans and finalize affected balances.
- The team is developing a proposal for a protocol-managed recovery fund and disclosed no funding terms or payout timetable.
Chainflip said on Nov. 27 that it had finished assessing how the theft from its Bitcoin and Ethereum vaults affected user balances.
The cross-chain swap protocol said the accounting gives it a basis to develop a recovery plan for people who were swapping at the time, regular account holders, and liquidity providers who supply assets for trades.
In its second incident report, Chainflip said it had finalized the list of affected users and the method for calculating the impact on each account. It said it will settle outstanding loans at prices from the time of the Nov. 21 attack to finalize affected balances.
The team said it could use the list to record the losses on-chain and set up a recovery fund managed by the protocol.
What the earlier Chainflip refunds covered
Chainflip’s first incident report valued the assets stolen from the two vaults at about $12.6 million using prices from the morning of the attack.
The new accounting looks at the impact on individual accounts, which is what Chainflip says will inform its recovery proposal.
Chainflip began returning free balances to liquidity providers on five unaffected networks while it assessed losses. The first report named Solana, Arbitrum, Tron, BNB Chain and Polkadot Asset Hub. Governance used designated refund addresses to send back those available funds.
The first report said assets in open loans, strategies, or range orders could still be held in Chainflip accounts, so a provider could receive a precautionary refund and still have assets in an open position.
Chainflip said the protocol remains paused pending security review and fixes. It said major active liquidity providers were willing to return if that work met a high standard and a plan to replenish their capital was put into effect.
Chainflip and the Crosschain Association are also working to add SwapKit to the existing swap site. That temporary service would route new trades through other providers while Chainflip works on its own restart.

articles.title: AI-Powered GTA 6 PC Ports Now Have Multiplayer as Modders Unlock 30 and 60 FPS
articles.text:
In brief
- Unofficial GTA 6 PC ports have reportedly achieved 25–30 frames per second, with developers already demonstrating multiplayer functionality and in-game mods.
- A separate patch allows jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles to exceed the game's official 30 FPS limit, targeting up to 60 FPS.
- A former Rockstar technical director warned that AI-assisted ports could force the company to accelerate its official PC release.
Gamers managed to get multiplayer working on GTA 6 for PC before Rockstar Games managed to release GTA 6 for PC. And they're apparently making the console version run better than the original, too.
A developer going by TeK shared footage Thursday showing multiple players interacting within the same game world in an unofficial PC build of Grand Theft Auto 6. The implementation reportedly supports character and vehicle synchronization, as well as proximity voice chat, running at between 25 and 30 frames per second (FPS).
GTA VI Working Multiplayer, Character, Vehicles & Proximity voice chat. (25-30FPS)#GTAVI #GTA6 pic.twitter.com/PyWvg764zZ
— TeK (@TeKGameR950) November 26, 2026
The development comes just a day after Decrypt reported that some AI-assisted ports were struggling to achieve 20 FPS while consuming upwards of 40 GB of system memory.
Another development team, known as BoYoo, demonstrated gameplay averaging 27 FPS during a boat mission, using an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor, an Nvidia RTX 5070 Ti graphics card, and 32 GB of RAM. Memory consumption dropped to approximately 15.4 GB, although performance in the more demanding downtown areas of Vice City remains untested.
No son 60 FPS en el GTA de los Mares del SUR en PS5 pero NADA MAL CHAVALES!! pic.twitter.com/L63ALb7JAu
— NanospeedGamer (@NanospeedGamer) November 26, 2026
Developers have also demonstrated in-game modification menus, allowing them to manipulate elements of the game for debugging purposes.
Meanwhile, console modders have released a patch that removes GTA 6's 30 FPS cap on jailbroken PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles. The latter reportedly exceeds 50 FPS during gameplay without relying on AI-generated intermediate frames.
The patch doesn't guarantee a consistent 60 FPS, but it does offer the potential for smoother gameplay and more responsive controls than Rockstar's officially supported version. For some players, modifying their console could arguably provide a better gameplay experience.
The advancements come despite Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, successfully taking down 3,007 GitHub repositories associated with Project Leonida, one of the most prominent efforts to bring the game to PC using AI coding tools.
Developers are using AI to reverse-engineer a leaked Xbox build of the game and adapt its code to run on computers, dramatically accelerating a process that traditionally required extensive manual work.
Could AI cost Rockstar money?
Rockstar has historically made PC gamers wait. Grand Theft Auto 5 arrived on PC in April 2015, roughly 19 months after its original console release, while Red Dead Redemption 2 took just over a year.
Generative AI could make that business strategy considerably riskier.
Obbe Vermeij, a former technical director at Rockstar North, warned about precisely this scenario before GTA 6's release.
“I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC,” Vermeij told Rock Paper Shotgun in an interview.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short NVDA with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Vermeij estimated that such an undertaking could cost tens of thousands of dollars in AI processing. Even if the resulting product fell short of Rockstar's official version, he suggested it could be good enough to satisfy some PC gamers, giving the company an incentive to bring its release dates closer together.
Wall Street has been paying attention, too.
During Take-Two's November 9 earnings call, Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok asked management how AI-assisted reverse engineering and decompilation were affecting the company's approach to security and development.
Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick acknowledged that piracy would become more challenging, although he maintained that replicating the intended experience of its games would remain technically difficult.
“I think it will be manageable, and we are focused on it,” Zelnick said.
There is some academic research suggesting that early piracy can substantially affect video game sales. A 2024 study published in Entertainment Computing by researcher William Volckmann examined games protected by Denuvo, an anti-piracy technology, and estimated average revenue losses of 20% when that protection was broken particularly early in a game's commercial life.
That figure cannot be directly extrapolated to GTA 6, which has yet to enter the PC market. But a sufficiently polished unofficial port distributed for free months before Rockstar's commercial release could reduce the number of players willing to pay full price for the same story they have already completed.
Rockstar would still have advantages, including official multiplayer servers, technical support, downloadable content, and a more polished gaming experience. The unofficial multiplayer implementation remains far removed from the scale of GTA Online, and none of the community projects has independently demonstrated that the entire campaign can be completed reliably.
GTA 6 generated an estimated $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day alone, according to a regulatory filing by Take-Two. Twenty percent of that would amount to roughly $758 million in lost sales revenue.
Rockstar still hasn't announced a PC release date.
